profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility on Northeast 62nd Avenue, Hillsboro, OR, per mapping data, with no house number on file. This session's fetch of Digital Realty's Portland metro property list did not conclusively match this coordinate to a specific named property, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Portland metro footprint, concentrated in Hillsboro, a Portland suburb that also hosts major semiconductor manufacturing and, per Digital Realty's own metro page, named properties PDX10 and PDX12 along Aloclek Drive and Schaaf Street. Portland General Electric serves most of the Hillsboro data center market, and Oregon offers enterprise-zone property tax abatements that Washington County and the City of Hillsboro have used to attract large industrial and data center investment. Digital Realty markets its Portland properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand within its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro market rather than per-building specifics for any US facility; this pattern of aggregate, not per-building, disclosure is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, and is not unique to this entry.

reading.body:
Digital Realty operates this facility on Northeast 62nd Avenue in Hillsboro, Oregon as part of its Portland metro portfolio, but has not published a megawatt capacity figure for this building. Digital Reality's FY2025 10-K discloses portfolio metrics by region and metropolitan market rather than per-building power ratings for any US facility, making the IT load here unknown from operator sources. The facility's specific operational status is unclear, as Digital Realty's current Portland property list names only PDX10 and PDX12, not this address.

Hillsboro sits in Washington County, which offers enterprise-zone property tax abatements that local coverage ties directly to data center buildout in the area. Portland General Electric serves most of the Hillsboro data center market. Oregon's published data center capacity totals 156.6 MW across eight facilities with disclosed figures, and only eight of 133 mapped facilities in the state publish power ratings at all, making Oregon's true colocation and wholesale IT footprint largely opaque from public spec pages.

Without a published megawatt figure, this campus cannot be ranked against other Oregon facilities or assessed for its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. The absence of capacity data reflects a structural pattern in this registry's session: Digital Realty discloses colocation supply at the metro and regional level as a business practice, not per building, limiting what a reader can infer about this site's role in the state's compute availability.
